description: OSTutorAI retrieval evaluation dataset. Labels the retrieval/grounding decision boundary against the CURRENT project-authored OS knowledge base (data/raw/*.md, 15 topic documents, ingested 2026-09-11). corpus_support labels were re-validated against that knowledge base on 2026-09-11 (schema_version 1 was relative to the old toy corpus).

label_history.corpus: 15 project-authored OS topic documents in data/raw/
label_history.note: The 15-document OS knowledge base covers every topic the relevant questions probe, so all borderline/partial and relevant/absent labels became covered. expected_relevance labels are UNCHANGED; only corpus_support and expected_source were re-derived from the actual corpus contents.

expected_relevance.relevant: A genuine Operating Systems question that OSTutorAI should be able to answer when the knowledge base covers the topic. Does NOT imply the current corpus covers it (see corpus_support).
expected_relevance.borderline: Question whose retrieval outcome is genuinely uncertain against this corpus (partial thematic overlap only). Excluded from precision/recall; reported separately.
expected_relevance.irrelevant: Clearly outside the Operating Systems tutoring scope (other domains, DSA, networking, career, trivia). Should always be rejected by the grounding gate.

corpus_support.covered: A document in data/raw/ explicitly contains the information needed to answer the question. Only covered+relevant questions are ground-truth positives.
corpus_support.partial: The corpus contains only thematically adjacent content; the question cannot be reliably answered from it.
corpus_support.absent: The corpus contains no supporting content for this question.

confusion_matrix_rules.excluded: borderline questions and relevant+absent questions (corpus coverage gaps) are reported separately and never counted in TP/FP/FN/TN

label_definitions.score_meaning: Retrieval score is cosine similarity (normalized embeddings, FAISS inner product) in [-1, 1]. It is NOT a percentage or probability. Labels are corpus-relative and MUST be re-validated whenever the knowledge base changes.

questions.question: In an operating system, what is a program in execution called?
questions.note: Answered by the process definition ('A process is a program in execution') in processes.md; os_fundamentals.md adds the program-vs-process distinction.

questions.question: What is a process in an operating system?
questions.note: processes.md contains the full definition, memory layout, states, PCB.

questions.question: What does a process own while it is executing?
questions.note: processes.md: address space, registers, PC, stack, PCB bookkeeping.

questions.question: How is a process related to a program?
questions.note: processes.md: 'A program is the passive executable file; one program can spawn many processes.'

questions.question: What is a deadlock in operating systems?
questions.note: deadlocks.md Definition section; scored 0.6915 under the toy corpus and 0.6408 under the new KB.

questions.question: What happens when a group of processes each hold a resource and wait for resources held by the others?
questions.note: Long paraphrase of the deadlock definition; deadlocks.md covers it with an explicit two-process example.

questions.question: Why might processes that wait on each other's resources never finish running?
questions.note: Paraphrase of permanent blocking; deadlocks.md explains none can proceed and none will release.

questions.question: How does the operating system decide which process gets the CPU next?
questions.note: cpu_scheduling.md defines scheduling as exactly this decision; under the toy corpus this scored 0.3422 (rejected); under the new KB the same intent scores 0.6069.

questions.question: What determines the order in which processes are allocated CPU time?
questions.note: Scheduling paraphrase; the previous FN at threshold 0.42 with the toy corpus. Re-scored against the new KB during recalibration.

questions.question: What is a thread in an operating system?
questions.note: Coverage update (v1->v2): threads.md now contains the full thread definition and private/shared resource split. Was absent under the toy corpus.

questions.question: How do threads differ from processes?
questions.note: Coverage update (v1->v2): threads.md has an explicit process-vs-thread comparison table.

questions.question: What is a semaphore used for in operating systems?
questions.note: Coverage update (v1->v2): synchronization.md explains wait/signal, binary and counting semaphores, resource pools.

questions.question: What is a critical section?
questions.note: Coverage update (v1->v2): synchronization.md defines critical sections and the three protocol requirements.

questions.question: What is paging in operating systems?
questions.note: Coverage update (v1->v2): memory_management.md has a full Paging section (pages/frames, page tables, TLB).

questions.question: How does the operating system manage memory allocation for processes?
questions.note: Coverage update (v1->v2): memory_management.md covers contiguous allocation, fragmentation, paging, segmentation.

questions.question: What is virtual memory?
questions.note: Coverage update (v1->v2): virtual_memory.md is entirely about virtual memory, demand paging, and replacement.

questions.question: What is a file system in an operating system?
questions.note: Coverage update (v1->v2): file_systems.md covers files, attributes, directories, allocation, free space.

questions.question: How does an operating system handle input and output devices?
questions.note: Coverage update (v1->v2): io_systems.md covers controllers, drivers, polling/interrupts/DMA, buffering, spooling.

questions.question: What are the necessary conditions for deadlock?
questions.note: Coverage update (v1->v2, was borderline/partial): deadlocks.md explicitly lists the four Coffman conditions and their sufficiency status.

questions.question: What is round-robin CPU scheduling?
questions.note: Coverage update (v1->v2, was borderline/partial): cpu_scheduling.md has a Round Robin section (quantum, convoy/degeneration trade-offs).

questions.question: What happens during a context switch?
questions.note: Coverage update (v1->v2, was borderline/partial): processes.md has a Context Switching section (what is saved, when it happens, its cost).

questions.question: Can threads within the same process share resources?
questions.note: Coverage update (v1->v2, was borderline/partial): threads.md lists exactly what threads share (code, data, heap, files) vs own (stack, registers).

questions.question: How can an operating system prevent processes from interfering with each other?
questions.note: Coverage update (v1->v2, was borderline/partial): synchronization.md covers mutual exclusion via Peterson, test-and-set, mutexes, semaphores, monitors; protection_security.md adds isolation.

questions.question: Where do processes keep their state while they are running?
questions.note: Coverage update (v1->v2, was borderline/partial): processes.md Process Memory Layout section (text, data, BSS, heap, stack) and the PCB (register state).

questions.question: Do processes need to wait for resources during input and output operations?
questions.note: Coverage update (v1->v2, was borderline/partial): processes.md state model includes Running->Blocked (waits for I/O) and io_systems.md explains blocking vs interrupt-driven transfers.

questions.question: Explain photosynthesis in plants.
questions.note: Biology; far from corpus semantics. Should be rejected.

questions.question: What is a binary search tree used for?
questions.note: DSA topic, intentionally out of scope; strongest-scoring negative under the toy corpus (0.3232). Re-scored against the new KB during recalibration.

questions.question: Explain the difference between TCP and UDP.
questions.note: Networking is out of scope. Coverage update (v1->v2): support changed partial->absent because the new KB correctly contains no networking content (the old toy corpus had one TCP sentence).

questions.note: ML; should be rejected.

questions.question: What is a foreign key in a database?
questions.note: DBMS is out of scope. Coverage update (v1->v2): support changed partial->absent (the old toy corpus had one DBMS sentence).
